then.text: Tell Úna I said hello and that her warp is still too tight. She'll know what I mean. She'll pretend she doesn't.

else.text: From Úna in Donegal Town? Then you'll want colour. Here: heather tips for a soft purple-grey, and whin, the gorse, for a yellow you could see from Tory.
Then the little flecks go in, the nepps, spun right into the yarn. That's what makes it Donegal. Off you go to Úna now, before the colours fade.
{greeting} Every cottage in the parish had a loom once. The women spun and dyed, the men wove, and the tweed went off to the merchants in the town.
Lichen, heather, gorse, blackberries, onion skins. A whole hillside goes into a good jacket. And a fair bit of the weaver, too.
